verdicts.why: Censorious weight on a failure of judgement fits 'foolish or senseless behavior', the contrast with craziness stays inside the word, and both examples use folly in this sense.
Note follows the gloss's clowning-and-buffoonery sense rather than the commoner lightness sense, and amused disapproval is a plausible negative charge.
Describes the mildest negative in the family without leaving the gloss; framing senseless behaviour as something allowed oneself is still disparaging, so the charge holds.
Insane rather than unwise is exactly the force of lunacy under this gloss, and the note stays on the word.
Sudden break-away with no blame fits 'moving with great haste' and the neutral charge; the contrast with hurry is a word-to-word one.
Short spirited burst against bolt's startled suddenness describes this sense, and 'made a dash for the door' fits it.

The example 'make haste and tell us; make haste, my love' is the set phrase for simply hurrying up and carries none of the carelessness this gloss requires, so it belongs to a different sense of haste; the note itself is acceptable.
Plain name for fast-and-careless with the carelessness carried quietly fits the gloss, and 'hurry and confusion' is this sense.
Momentum overriding care is a fair reading of the careless-hurry gloss and differentiates it from hurry inside the word.
Describes what the gerund form does to the same careless speed relative to rush, staying within the gloss.
Small skittering hurry that reads as comic rather than damning matches 'undignified' and a mild negative charge.
Graceless effortful floundering is the undignified hurry of the gloss, distinguished from scamper on force alone.
Praise for not wavering across purpose, devotion and affection tracks the gloss word for word, and all four examples fit.
Cool report of not changing with no credit for holding fast fits 'constant and unchanging' and the neutral charge; 'immutable laws of nature' is this sense.
Firmness others can lean on is the 'firm and dependable' of the gloss, and the comparison with constant stays inside the words.
Never running out is a fair picture of 'tireless', the charge is positive, and both examples fit.
Pace that never slackens versus a store that never empties differentiates it from unfailing on the same 'tireless' gloss.
Relentless repetition foregrounded over instruction fits 'instill by constant repetition' with a negative charge, and both examples are this sense.
Repetition and admonition in the service of teaching is the gloss restated with register; neutral charge is plausible.
Offhand expectation resting on little is the 'suppose' reading of the gloss, and the example uses it that way.
Belief reached by picturing, more speculative than think, fits 'expect, believe, or suppose' and all three examples.
Formal register and belief-as-opinion-delivered stays on the word and within the gloss.
Informal is a register label, and 'flatly settled' against suppose's tentativeness is a difference inside the word.
Provisional belief granted rather than asserted fits the gloss, and both examples are this sense.
Belief aimed at someone and against them is 'hold in suspicion; believe to be guilty', negative charge fits, and the example matches.
Plain unmarked belief without suppose's hedge or opine's formality fits the gloss, and the examples are the expect/suppose sense.
Approval at its floor tracks the 'minimal adherence, sufficient but not noteworthy' gloss, and 'more than civil; really attentive' shows exactly that floor.
Usages kept rather than offence avoided, with consideration that stays unremarkable, follows the gloss and differentiates from civil inside the word.
